requirement: Prompt Refiner의 승인된 one-run 계약을 실제로 수행할 수 있는 owner-only, default-off staging shadow runner를 구현한다. 시작·resume마다 DB-clock stale-intent sweep과 exact stage/run/runtime/expiry 검증을 수행하고, frozen synthetic corpus 16건을 순차적으로 reservation -> durable dispatch intent/consume -> 고정 provider adapter -> immutable terminal receipt 순서로만 처리한다. js-tiktoken 1.0.21의 o200k_base 계수를 dispatch 전에 강제하며 tokenizer identity와 count를 audit에 결속한다. retry, redispatch, fallback, parallel dispatch, 제품 Chat 연결, prompt/output 저장은 금지한다. maintenance는 sweeper만 호출하고 provider 경계에는 도달할 수 없어야 한다. 이 변경은 flag 활성화, stage/run 생성, provider 호출, 유료 실행 또는 제품 공개를 수행하지 않는다. author는 codex, reviewer는 claude이며 Claude Code Max 구독 CLI의 읽기 전용 도구만 사용한다.
completionCriteria: run contract v3는 actual tokenizer identity, exact 16-case order, 100000 input cap, 4096 output cap, 15000ms timeout, 240000ms invocation admission budget, 10000ms terminal-write margin, retry 0, 요청당/전체 비용 ceiling과 stop-no-redispatch를 고정하고 productAdapterReady=false를 유지한다.
owner-only execute GET/POST는 recent authentication, no-store, origin guard, DB rate limit, 4 KiB strict JSON, exact run id/digest/confirmation을 강제하며 product prompt나 model output을 반환하지 않는다.

runner는 첫 동작으로 DB-clock sweeper를 실행하고 unresolved incident나 in-flight intent에서 새 dispatch를 만들지 않는다. 각 terminal 뒤와 다음 case 시작 전에 default-off kill switch를 다시 확인하되, 이미 dispatch한 case의 terminal 기록은 kill switch로 건너뛰지 않는다.
각 case는 exact reservation과 durable intent가 성공한 뒤에만 provider adapter에 도달한다. pre-intent failure는 reservation을 한 번 release하고, post-intent 또는 terminal-write 불명 결과는 retry·redispatch 없이 중단한다.
frozen 16건은 corpus order대로 한 번씩만 실행되며 unknown_after_dispatch가 하나라도 있으면 run latch 뒤 다음 case를 시작하지 않는다. transient refined prompt는 durable store나 route 응답에 남지 않는다.

js-tiktoken@1.0.21 o200k_base가 system/user content를 계수하고 fixed framing 32를 더한 admission count를 dispatch 전에 검사한다. DB trigger는 tokenizer package/version/encoding과 0..100000 count가 결속된 system audit만 허용한다.
15분 maintenance는 durable sweeper만 import·호출하며 runner/live adapter/provider를 import하지 않는다. kill switch와 무관하게 stale intent를 unknown으로 닫되 새 reservation·dispatch를 생성하지 않는다.
v3 migration은 기존 run/attempt가 있으면 fail-closed하고 v3 contract/audit constraints만 교체하며 어떤 승인·attempt도 seed하지 않는다.
unit, server-contract, DB integration, typecheck, 대상 lint, 문서·정책·encoding·security·runtime source closure 검사가 통과한다.
Claude Code Max는 사용자가 승인한 skip-preflight 예외 아래 Read·Grep·Glob만으로 고정 digest를 독립 검토하며 Anthropic API key를 사용하지 않는다. 최초 검토와 최대 2회 수정 검토만 허용한다.

findings.claim: The pinned admission tokenizer `js-tiktoken` is declared only as a devDependency, yet it is now a static runtime import on the shipped paid-dispatch path (execute/route.ts -> promptRefinerShadowRunner.ts:11 -> promptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter.ts:33 -> promptRefinerShadowTokenizer.ts:3), so it is excluded from the repo's production vulnerability audit and from any dev-omitting install.
findings.reproduction: grep -n 'js-tiktoken' package.json -> line 309 is inside the devDependencies block (lines 300-314); package-lock.json:10184-10188 shows `"dev": true`. Before this change the only importer was scripts/report-token-estimate-accuracy.mjs:32 (a dev script). Consequence 1: .github/workflows/daily-security-audit.yml:113 runs `npm audit --omit=dev`, so any future CVE in a package that now executes inside app/api/admin/prompt-refiner/shadow-run/execute/route.ts is invisible to that audit. Consequence 2: `npm ci --omit=dev && npx next build` fails to resolve `js-tiktoken` from lib/promptRefinerShadowTokenizer.ts. Fix: move `js-tiktoken` into `dependencies` and regenerate package-lock.json (the frozen-version assertion in tests/promptRefinerShadowTokenizer.test.mjs:19 still holds).

findings.claim: The sequential loop has no wall-clock budget guard against the route's `maxDuration = 300`, so a worst-case invocation can be killed between a durable intent and its terminal write, which permanently latches the one-run authority to `stopped_unknown`.
findings.reproduction: Arithmetic against the frozen contract: 16 cases x PROMPT_REFINER_TIMEOUT_MS 15000 = 240s of provider budget alone, plus ~65 DB transactions (16 reserve, 16 intent, 16 terminal, 17 readState) and ~33 full run-source-manifest builds (readRunSourceFiles at lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:206-227 re-reads and hashes all 14 paths, including package-lock.json, on every recordPromptRefinerShadowDispatchIntent and readPromptRefinerShadowExecutionState). At 30-80ms RTT that overhead alone is tens of seconds, so total can exceed the 300s cap. If the platform kills the function while an attempt is in `dispatch_intent`, sweepPromptRefinerShadowUnknowns closes it as `unknown_after_dispatch` (lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:1000-1006), the run trigger makes `stopped_unknown` immutable (20260920120000 migration.sql:310-312), and `PromptRefinerShadowRun_runContractDigest_key` (same file, line 84) forbids a replacement run without a new contract digest. Suggested fix: record a start timestamp in the runner and return `paused` before reserving a case when remaining budget < timeoutMs + write margin.

findings.claim: The runner validates the bundled corpus only for self-consistency and never binds it to the frozen PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_CORPUS_DIGEST, so the exact bytes it sends to the provider are verified only indirectly via a different (on-disk) copy.
findings.reproduction: lib/promptRefinerShadowHarness.ts:405 compares the recomputed digest against the file's own embedded `contentDigest` field, never against PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_CORPUS_DIGEST (lib/promptRefinerShadowHarness.ts:29). The frozen-digest binding exists only in the stage-admission path, which reads the file from process.cwd() (lib/promptRefinerStageAdmission.ts:202, lib/promptRefinerShadowAdmissionCore.ts:734-741), while the runner dispatches `item.sourceText` from the webpack-bundled import at lib/promptRefinerShadowRunner.ts:5. Edit any `sourceText` in docs/ops/prompt-refiner-shadow/corpus-v1.json and update its `contentDigest` field, then call createPromptRefinerShadowRunner with stubbed store deps: the runner accepts and dispatches the altered text. Fix: `if (corpus.contentDigest !== PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_CORPUS_DIGEST) throw ...` next to line 29.

findings.claim: The new maintenance-step mock returns a sweeper shape the real export never produces, so the added assertions (`examined`, `closedUnknown`) do not exercise the real sweeper's contract.
findings.reproduction: Compare the mock's `{ examined, closedUnknown, completedRuns, unresolvedStaleAttemptIds, consumedWithoutAttempt }` with the real return at lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:1095-1103, which is `{ observedAt, staleCandidates, closedUnknownAttemptIds, unresolvedStaleAttemptIds, consumedWithoutAttempt, retryCount, redispatched }`. `examined`, `closedUnknown` and `completedRuns` do not exist on the real value, so `result.promptRefinerShadowUnknowns?.examined === 2` (test line ~403) would keep passing after any incompatible change to the sweeper's return shape. Fix: mock the real field names.

findings.claim: GET enforces no DB rate limit even though it performs a full source-manifest read and takes `FOR UPDATE` row locks plus a share lock on ModelRegistryEntry on every call.
findings.reproduction: route.ts GET calls readPromptRefinerShadowExecutionState() with no consumeApiRateLimit; tests/server-contract/admin-prompt-refiner-shadow-execution-route.test.ts asserts `world.rateLimitCalls === 0` for GET. Each call runs readRunSourceFiles (14 files incl. package-lock.json) and lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:400-407 (`lockStage` FOR UPDATE, `LOCK TABLE "ModelRegistryEntry" IN SHARE MODE`, run FOR UPDATE). The completion criterion lists the DB rate limit for 'execute GET/POST'; add a read-scoped limit or state explicitly that it is POST-only.

rounds.nextAction: Move js-tiktoken to production dependencies and regenerate the lockfile; the three warnings (invocation budget guard, corpus digest binding, maintenance mock shape) are cheap follow-ups that should land in the same revision.

findings.claim: The new invocation budget can force a second POST to finish the 16 cases, but the POST bucket allows only 2 calls per day and is consumed before validation, so a single rejected or wasted POST inside the 60-minute approval window can strand the one-run authority permanently after paid dispatches.
findings.reproduction: Arithmetic on the shipped constants: if every case hits the 15,000 ms provider timeout, case k starts at ~(k-1)*15,000 ms; the guard at lib/promptRefinerShadowRunner.ts:171-176 pauses once elapsed > 240,000-15,000-10,000 = 215,000 ms, i.e. before case 15, so the run needs a 2nd POST. Observable in the unit test by extending tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs with `nowMs` advancing 15,500 ms per call: the result is `status: "paused"` with `attemptedThisInvocation < 16`. Meanwhile, in tests/server-contract/admin-prompt-refiner-shadow-execution-route.test.ts the three invalid POSTs in "POST accepts only the exact 4 KiB execution binding" each reach `consumeApiRateLimit` before `readLimitedJson` (assert `world.rateLimitCalls === 3` there to see it), so wrong-body or 503 attempts burn the same 2/day quota that the resume needs, and lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts refuses once `run.approvalExpiresAt <= now` (60 min), leaving the run below 16 terminals with no legal resume.

findings.claim: The runner fixture's sweeper fake returns `{ examined, closedUnknown, completedRuns, ... }`, a shape lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:1095-1103 never produces (it returns `staleCandidates`/`closedUnknownAttemptIds`), so the runner's declared `sweep: typeof sweepPromptRefinerShadowUnknowns` dependency is not pinned by the test — the same class of drift that was fixed for the maintenance test this round.
findings.reproduction: Compare tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs:41-47 with the real return object at lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:1095-1103; only `unresolvedStaleAttemptIds` and `consumedWithoutAttempt` exist in both. Replacing the fake with the real field names keeps the test green, which shows the extra keys assert nothing.

findings.claim: On the defensive `INTENT_MISSING` path (adapter resolved without ever invoking `onDispatch`) the runner refuses without releasing the reservation it just took, leaving a `reserved` row to age out instead of being closed once like the pre-intent path does.
findings.reproduction: In tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs, add a fixture whose `adapter` resolves an outcome without calling `onDispatch`: `run()` rejects with `PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_INTENT_MISSING` and `events` contains `reserve:...` but no `release`.

findings.claim: Every failure path in the one-run runner discards the causal error without binding it, logging it, or reporting an incident, so a halted paid shadow leaves only a generic code (`PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_PRE_DISPATCH_FAILED` / `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` / `TERMINAL_WRITE_UNKNOWN`) and no record of why, in a system that forbids retrying to find out.
findings.reproduction: `rg -n 'console\.|reportOperationalIncident' lib/promptRefinerShadowRunner.ts` returns nothing, and both catch clauses bind no error variable. The route cannot compensate: app/api/admin/prompt-refiner/shadow-run/execute/route.ts:152-153 returns `promptRefinerShadowRunnerErrorResponse(error)` before ever reaching its `console.error` at line 160. Concretely, tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs `failAfterIntentAt` throws `new Error("after intent")` and the only observable output is the 503 code — the message reaches no sink. lib/maintenance.ts:26 shows the project's existing `reportOperationalIncident` channel for exactly this class of event.

findings.claim: When `recordPromptRefinerShadowDispatchIntent` returns `reservation_expired` it has already transitioned the row to `expired`, so the runner's subsequent release necessarily fails and the operator is told `PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_PRE_DISPATCH_RELEASE_FAILED` ("could not close its reservation") about a reservation that is in fact correctly closed.
findings.reproduction: lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:782-786 sets `status: "expired"` and returns `{ok:false, reason:"reservation_expired"}`; that `!intent.ok` branch (runner line 205-211) throws inside `onDispatch`, so the runner's catch at line 215 sees `attemptId === null` and calls `dependencies.release(reservation)`. lib/promptRefinerReservationAuthority.ts:316 refuses any non-`reserved` row with `reservation_not_active`, so `released.ok` is false and the runner refuses with the release-failure code instead of the real `reservation_expired` cause. No test covers this path: tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs has no fixture where `recordIntent` returns `ok:false`.

findings.claim: The budget guard compares against the literal `300_000` rather than the route's declared `maxDuration`, so lowering `export const maxDuration` would leave a 240 s admission budget that exceeds the platform cap with no gate failing.
findings.reproduction: Change `export const maxDuration = 300;` to `60` in app/api/admin/prompt-refiner/shadow-run/execute/route.ts and run `npm run test:prompt-refiner-shadow-live-adapter`; it stays green, and `promptRefinerShadowRunContractProblems()` still returns `[]`. tests/cronClientTimeouts.test.mjs:52 shows the project's existing idiom for parsing `export const maxDuration` out of a route and binding it to an in-code budget.

findings.claim: Every failure path in the one-run runner discards the causal error without binding it, logging it, or reporting an incident, so a halted paid shadow leaves only a generic code (`PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_PRE_DISPATCH_FAILED` / `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` / `TERMINAL_WRITE_UNKNOWN`) and no record of why, in a system that forbids retrying to find out.
findings.reproduction: `rg -n 'console\.|reportOperationalIncident' lib/promptRefinerShadowRunner.ts` returns nothing, and both catch clauses bind no error variable. The route cannot compensate: app/api/admin/prompt-refiner/shadow-run/execute/route.ts:152-153 returns `promptRefinerShadowRunnerErrorResponse(error)` before ever reaching its `console.error` at line 160. Concretely, tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs `failAfterIntentAt` throws `new Error("after intent")` and the only observable output is the 503 code — the message reaches no sink. lib/maintenance.ts:26 shows the project's existing `reportOperationalIncident` channel for exactly this class of event.

findings.claim: When `recordPromptRefinerShadowDispatchIntent` returns `reservation_expired` it has already transitioned the row to `expired`, so the runner's subsequent release necessarily fails and the operator is told `PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_PRE_DISPATCH_RELEASE_FAILED` ("could not close its reservation") about a reservation that is in fact correctly closed.
findings.reproduction: lib/promptRefinerShadowRunStore.ts:782-786 sets `status: "expired"` and returns `{ok:false, reason:"reservation_expired"}`; that `!intent.ok` branch (runner line 205-211) throws inside `onDispatch`, so the runner's catch at line 215 sees `attemptId === null` and calls `dependencies.release(reservation)`. lib/promptRefinerReservationAuthority.ts:316 refuses any non-`reserved` row with `reservation_not_active`, so `released.ok` is false and the runner refuses with the release-failure code instead of the real `reservation_expired` cause. No test covers this path: tests/promptRefinerShadowRunner.test.mjs has no fixture where `recordIntent` returns `ok:false`.

findings.claim: The budget guard compares against the literal `300_000` rather than the route's declared `maxDuration`, so lowering `export const maxDuration` would leave a 240 s admission budget that exceeds the platform cap with no gate failing.
findings.reproduction: Change `export const maxDuration = 300;` to `60` in app/api/admin/prompt-refiner/shadow-run/execute/route.ts and run `npm run test:prompt-refiner-shadow-live-adapter`; it stays green, and `promptRefinerShadowRunContractProblems()` still returns `[]`. tests/cronClientTimeouts.test.mjs:52 shows the project's existing idiom for parsing `export const maxDuration` out of a route and binding it to an in-code budget.
